Quick update — we pulled the serving and control-plane logs for the time range. Preliminary findings:

- Control plane: 2028-12-02 19:12:41–19:14:07 UTC: transient auth service latency spike (internal token exchange) causing ~4.1% of requests to error with 503s while retry logic was hit.
- Serving/runtime: 19:15:10–19:17:05 UTC: short-lived queuing on the payment-scoring route in us-west-2 due to an unexpected burst from a public demo tenant; peaks coincided with customer window and increased tail latency.
- Around 19:20 UTC there were several retries and a routed fallback to a quantized model variant which increased response times but avoided complete failure for most requests.

Attachments: redwood-logs-20281202-peakwindow.tar.gz (trimmed logs), sla_calc_initial.xlsx (internal calc snapshot).

I'll assemble a tight CSV for Dana with timestamps and response codes and share next. From a quick SLA standpoint, the control-plane auth latency meets our internal incident severity threshold but the combination of auth spike + tenant burst looks like it produced a marginal partial outage for a subset of requests. Need Product to weigh in on whether that meets contractual "unavailable" definition for credit.
